release.notes:
**Memory in long sessions, video profiles, Safe Launch and Quick settings, and homebrew in the Library.** Tears of the Kingdom ended after about an hour on v1.010.006 and slowed down after its item menu: Nightshade kept 2 GB more of the console's memory than it used and never gave any back, and the game's largest texture needed one 176 MiB block that a long session no longer had. Nightshade now gives its memory back, uploads large textures in pieces, and its graphics caches no longer evict at their hardest for the rest of a session. Choose Minimum, Recommended, High or Ultra for every game or for one, start a game once in safe mode when it won't start, and change a game's video from a quick panel. Homebrew NROs are listed beside your games with their own names and icons, and newer games' ZBIC-compressed code must decode whole. Not confirmed on a console yet: play TOTK as long as you can, open its item menu often, and send `/data/prosperoeden/logs`.

### New

- **Video profiles.** **Settings > Video > Video profile** sets the resolution, upscaling filter, ASTC textures, **Faster GPU emulation** and **Asynchronous shaders** at once: **Minimum** (0.75x with AMD FSR, the faster GPU accuracy, asynchronous shaders), **Recommended** (1x, Bilinear: what a new install has), **High** (1.5x, Bicubic) and **Ultra** (2x, Bicubic). Each turns frame generation and post-processing off, and keeps ASTC textures compressed. A game's own Video has the same row, first: a profile chosen there is that game's own. Change one of those settings by hand and the profile shows **Custom**. Tears of the Kingdom has profiles of its own that keep the console's 4 GiB and compressed textures in every one, what v1.010.005 found it needs. See [Video profiles](https://github.com/Oliv3rmoon/Nightshade/blob/v1.010.007/docs/SETTINGS.md#video-profiles).
- **Quick settings.** Options on a game, in the Library, on the home screen or on its settings page, opens a panel with **Play**, **Start in safe mode**, its video profile, resolution, upscaling filter, renderer, FPS overlay and frame generation. A change is saved for that game at once; Triangle opens all of its settings.

apps.name: Physalis
apps.summary: Live TV, IPTV and Plex on PS5. Formerly Nightshade TV, built on ProsperoTV.
apps.author: Oliv3rmoon

release.notes:
**Physalis v1.002.005: MPEG-2 channels.** Channels in MPEG-2 play, a channel that can't play says what it is, and a new version is found while Physalis stays on.

## What changed

- **MPEG-2 channels.** Channels and videos in MPEG-2, as many standard-definition broadcast channels are, now play, and so does the older MPEG-1. The PS5's video decoder has no MPEG-2, so Physalis decodes it on the console's processor, up to 1920 × 1080. Interlaced channels are shown field by field to keep their motion, and a 4:3 or 16:9 picture is shown at the shape the channel gives it. In MPEG-TS, HLS, MP4 and Matroska. With **Stats line** on, it says MPEG2.
- **Why a channel didn't play.** A live channel whose video Physalis can't decode said only "The channel uses an unsupported media format." It now says what the channel sent, such as "The channel uses an unsupported media format: the programme has no supported video (stream type 0x10).", and the failure report saved to USB keeps the stream types.
- **New versions while it stays on.** Physalis looked for a new version only when it started. It now looks again every four hours while it stays on, only while you're in the menu, never while a channel or video plays: a check that comes due while you watch waits until you're back. A version you put off with **Later** isn't offered again until Physalis is started again.

## Install

- `PPSA99003.zip`: choose **Update now** when Physalis offers this release, or extract the ZIP and copy its `PPSA99003` folder over your current one (usually `/data/homebrew/PPSA99003`). Your sources, favorites and settings stay.
- `SHA256SUMS`: the checksum of the download. `gh attestation verify PPSA99003.zip -R Oliv3rmoon/Physalis` checks that this repository's workflow built it.

## Thanks

To **BlackBearReloaded**, who created ProsperoTV, and to **ThatGuyKalvin** and everyone who carries it on and tests it.

apps.name: Kodi
apps.summary: Kodi media center ported to the PS5, with the Estuary skin and the official Kodi add-on repository.
apps.author: Notedop

release.notes:
# Release Notes

## PS5-Specific Changes

- **PS5 Media Remote support:** Navigate Kodi, open playback controls, pause and resume, rewind, and fast-forward using the PS5 Media Remote.
- **More reliable remote reconnection:** Playback controls recover after the remote disconnects, without interrupting controller input.
- **Correct video pausing:** Pausing holds the displayed picture instead of allowing video frames to continue advancing. Frame-by-frame stepping remains available.
- **Improved VP9 playback:** More reliable playback after seeking or recovering from an interruption.
- **Improved video stability:** Safer transitions when hardware playback falls back to another playback method.
- **Expanded optional add-on support:** Added PS5 support for RTMP streams, SFTP file access, RAR and other archive formats, and PDF viewing. These add-ons are intended for the PS5 testing repository, are not bundled, and still require on-console validation.

## Upstream Changes

These changes were merged from Kodi's upstream Piers branch. Not all changes may apply to the PS5 platform.

### Video Playback and Subtitles

- Improved navigation between chapters, bookmarks, and scene markers, with large skips when no markers are available.
- More accurate seeking and automatic commercial skipping, including avoiding brief glimpses of adverts when seeking into a marked commercial break.
- Improved Blu-ray playback continuity and menu reliability, including keeping menus visible and separate from subtitles.
- Improved audio/video synchronization when using audio passthrough.
- Easier subtitle browsing, with direct access to the current video's folder and correctly listed local drives.

### Movies, TV Shows, and Library Management

- **Safer library refreshes:** Movies remain in the library when their details cannot be retrieved.
- Improved handling of multi-disc movies, including grouping matching discs into one library entry when automatic grouping is enabled.
- More reliable scanning and refreshing of disc images and Blu-ray/DVD folder backups.
- Corrected matching of artwork, trailers, subtitles, and external audio to the appropriate movie version, extra, episode, or disc.
- Improved local metadata discovery and reduced unnecessary rescanning after refreshing movies or episodes.
- Fixed upgrades from older libraries that could incorrectly turn movie versions into extras or leave the movie library empty.

### Pictures, Browsing, and Reliability

- **Correct HEIF and AVIF photo display:** Large tiled photos, including many iPhone images, now display completely rather than showing only part of the picture. Image rotation is also handled correctly.
- Reduced memory use when loading large JPEGs and browsing artwork.

release.notes:
## Media Player Classic PS5 1.6.1

Dark mode for the PS5 interface, with saved preferences and instant switching. The application version is
1.6.1, content version is 01.061.000, and the title ID remains PPSA99015.

### New

- **Dark mode:** choose **View > Options > Player > Theme > Dark**, then **Apply** or **OK**. Select **Light** to
  restore the original appearance. Existing settings use Light by default.
- **Immediate switching:** the window, toolbar, menus, playlist, file browser, dialogs and controls update without
  restarting the player. The choice is saved for the next launch. Cancel discards a choice that has not been applied.
- **Readable toolbar icons:** dark neutral glyphs are brightened for Dark, while colored icons and transparency
  retain their original values. Returning to Light restores the original toolbar pixels.
- **Independent video colors:** video, HDR processing, subtitles and custom subtitle colors retain their colors.

With a controller, use L1/R1 to move between controls, D-pad Left/Right to select the theme, and Cross on Apply or OK.

### Fixed

- Added missing Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, French and German translations for four existing HDR/GPU labels.
  The GPU retry button and hint are checked against the actual font metrics in all five languages.
- Fixed spaces in the dependency archive command and runtime checksum path. `MPCPS5_DEPS_DIR` allows dependencies
  to be built in a separate cache without spaces.
- Fixed an unused constant stopping Linux builds with Clang and `-Werror`, preserving the console's crash handling.

### Updating

- **From 1.6.0:** use **Help > Check for updates**, install the update and restart the app. The update ZIP contains
  the native application, its metadata, artwork, runtime module and file manifest.
- For manual installation, run `MediaPlayerClassicPS5-v1.6.1.elf` with your existing homebrew setup, then open
  Media Player Classic PS5 from the home screen. The ELF includes the installer, helper and native player.
- If an older installer ELF is configured in autoload, replace that file with the new installer.
- Settings and media remain in `/data/mpcps5`. The new preference is `DarkMode=1` (Dark) or `DarkMode=0` (Light)
  in `mpc-hc.ini`.

### Files

- `MediaPlayerClassicPS5-v1.6.1.elf`: the complete installer. This is the only ELF download for this release.
- `MediaPlayerClassicPS5-v1.6.1-PPSA99015.zip`: the application update package used by Help > Check for updates.
- `mpc-ps5-v1.6.1-src.zip`: the source code, tests, third-party notices and documentation.
- The `.sha256` files and `SHA256SUMS.txt`: download checksums.

### Validation and limits

apps.summary: Movie library that finds films in a movies folder on internal or USB storage, fetches posters from TMDB and plays them.
apps.author: M0S4YSH3LL0

release.notes:
## Mediathek 1.0.0 (`01.000.100`)

A Netflix-style library and player for your movies and series on the PS5. Put your films in a `movies` folder and your series in `tvshows` on the internal drive, a USB stick or extended storage; Mediathek finds them, shows a billboard and shelves with their posters, fetches covers and descriptions from TMDB, and plays them. English and German.

### What's new in 1.0.0

- **Hardware decoding at every size.** H.264 and HEVC films of every size now play on the console's video decoder, as in VLC's PS5 port, not only those beyond 1080p: it leaves the CPU and memory free and plays 1080p 10-bit HEVC that was heavy for the CPU. FFmpeg still decodes every other codec and takes over from where the film is when the hardware refuses one. `HW_DECODE=0` keeps everything on FFmpeg.
- **Subtitles inside the film.** Text tracks (SubRip, ASS/SSA as plain text, mov_text, WebVTT) and picture tracks (PGS from Blu-rays, VobSub from DVDs, DVB), drawn where the disc puts them and above the controls while those show. Triangle steps through the film's own tracks and the `.srt` files together, your language first; the message says which ("German · embedded", "German · SRT", "English · SDH · embedded"). The details page lists the languages of both.
- **Forced subtitles** (only the lines in another language than the film's: a sign, a scene abroad) show by themselves while no full subtitles are on, in your *Subtitle language*, or with None in the language of the sound playing. A file named `Film.de.forced.srt` counts too.
- **HDR output.** On a TV the console already sends HDR to, an HDR film is sent as HDR10 while it plays instead of being tone-mapped to SDR; the controls and subtitles are drawn over it at their usual brightness.
- **5.1 and 7.1 sound** on the console's 8-channel output instead of a stereo mix; the console mixes it down itself for a TV or headset with two channels. Menu sounds play in front.
- **New settings under Playback**, now grouped under Subtitles, Audio and Video: *Subtitle source* (Automatic, Embedded only, SRT only), *HDR output* (Automatic, Off), *Audio output* (Automatic, Stereo) and *Audio language* (Automatic, German, English: the main track in that language, not a commentary).
- Fixed: when the graphics chip cannot convert the hardware's pictures and the CPU does it, a film at its own size is no longer softened by half a pixel.

### Features

- **Home:** a billboard for the focused title, tinted by its colours, and one shelf at a time: Continue Watching, Recently Added, collections, one per genre, decades, All Movies and All Series.

apps.name: OliSe Player
apps.summary: Tracker-music radio streaming MOD, XM, S3M and IT modules from The Mod Archive, with MilkDrop visuals.
apps.author: Marice

release.notes:
Two archives to listen to, and a scroller that tells you what is playing.

## Modland as a second source

Triangle now asks which archive first, then which station. The two are kept
apart because they are organised differently: the Mod Archive by genre and
chart, Modland by curated playlist.

Modland is read through its playlists, which are plain text files of direct
links. Eight stations: the favourites of around 850 modules, a chiptune
selection, netlabel releases, a couple of musicdisks and a demoparty compo.

## The scroller says what is playing

The greeting runs its one pass at startup and is never cut short. After that
the band carries the track: title, source, the tracker that wrote the module,
channels, instruments, patterns, running time, and the genre and artist where
the archive gave them. A new track fades the band out, swaps the line and
fades it back in.

## Visualiser

Stepping through presets follows a shuffled order instead of the alphabet.
Sorted by filename, stepping meant working through one author at a time. The
visualiser also moves on by itself every minute; L2 + Options turns that off.

## Keep a track

L2 + Circle writes the playing module into `music/` and adds it to
`index.txt`, so a tune that would otherwise scroll out of the 20 track history
can be kept.

## Fixed

The interface named The Mod Archive everywhere, including while downloading
from Modland. Each track now carries where it came from.

## Installing

Copy the contents of `PPSA01153.zip` to `/data/homebrew/PPSA01153/`, reload
the jailbreak chain and start it from the home screen. The 552 MilkDrop
presets are in the zip; `OliSePlayer-presets.zip` is the same pack on its own,
for adding to an install made without it.

Drop your own modules in `music/` and add their names to `music/index.txt`:
the sandbox will not let the app list a folder, so it reads that index.

release.notes:
Twispero 1.1.0 puts a live picture on Home, adds a stream language filter and chat replies, and fixes a crash when closing from the PS button menu and sound and picture drifting apart.

### New

- Home's top stream plays live in its picture, without sound. Press X to watch it. It stops after 90 seconds without a button press, and Settings > Twitch can turn it off.
- Pick a stream language with L1 and R1 on Browse or on a category's Live tab. Home's Popular now row and every category's live streams follow it.
- Reply to a chat message. L1 pauses chat on the newest message, Up and Down pick another one, and L1 again opens the keyboard. This needs a Twitch login.
- Audio only for live streams in the quality menu (R2)

### Fixed

- Closing the app from the PS button menu while something played could crash the console. The app now stops drawing the moment the PS5 takes over, which happens before the close goes through.
- Audio and video drifting apart after the stream buffers on a slow connection (#1). Thanks to jumboz95 for reporting it.
- A blank line where a title is all Japanese, Korean or Chinese. The app still can't show those characters, so it skips the line now.
- Twitch's "processing" picture on a past broadcast that's still being recorded. It shows the live picture now.

### Known issues

- Channel points, and following or unfollowing a channel, aren't possible; Twitch only allows them in its own apps
- No chat replay on videos

release.notes:
## PSP5 01.000.100

PSP5 now follows the console's language, reads games and texture packs from USB drives, and lets you remap the PSP's buttons.

### Interface language

Choose a language under **Settings → System → Language** and the home screen follows it, not just the emulator. 45 languages are available, including Japanese, Korean, Chinese, Arabic, Hebrew, Thai and Lao. The font atlases were rebuilt to carry them, growing from 113 glyphs to 3,055 per face. Right-to-left languages are laid out right-to-left.

Where PPSSPP already translates a term, PSP5 uses its translation. The remainder — favourites, the A–Z view, the cheat panel, the save-state slots, the button names and the description under every settings row — are PSP5's own, shipped as 78 strings in 44 languages under `assets/lang/psp5/`.

**These 78 strings are machine-translated and unreviewed in most languages.** Corrections are a one-line edit in `assets/lang/psp5/<id>.ini`: the files are plain `English = translation`, and a missing line falls back to English.

### Games and texture packs on USB drives

PSP5 now reads drives using the same layout as its own memory stick:

```
/mnt/usb0/PSP/GAME/<your game>.iso        # also .cso, .chd, EBOOT.PBP
/mnt/usb0/PSP/TEXTURES/<DISC_ID>/         # a texture pack, with its textures.ini
```

All eight USB ports (`/mnt/usb0` … `/mnt/usb7`) and both extended drives (`/mnt/ext0`, `/mnt/ext1`) are scanned. A texture pack on a drive takes precedence over one on the memory stick.

**This requires folder listing to be unlocked.** A PS5 app can open a file by its full path but cannot list a folder, and finding games requires listing. PSP5 requests the unlock at every start, and any of these will grant it: **etaHEN** (enable *Legacy CMD server* in its toolbox), **OnionHEN**, **LegacyJB**, or the **PS5SX2 Helper** (add PSP5 to its `/data/whitelist.txt`).

Without it, PSP5 runs from its own memory stick as before and USB drives appear empty. The reason is recorded in `psp5.log` as `unlock: nothing answered`.

### Button remapping

**Settings → Controls → Buttons** lists all twelve PSP buttons — the four face buttons, both shoulders, Start, Select and the four D-pad directions — with the console button each is mapped to.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Cross** | set the button |
| **Square** | set a second button |
| **Triangle** | clear the second |
| **Circle** | back |

Each PSP button can be mapped to **two** console buttons, so Select can sit on both the touch pad and L3, or L on both L1 and L2.

# PS5X360 v1.0.2

Online play now gets past the start on the PS5, the emulator speaks every language it lists, a dark
theme, a Windows app that installs DLC and title updates over the network, and the Helper 1.3.0.
Compatibility keeps improving, but results depend on the game, firmware and homebrew setup.

## Online play (experimental)

Turn it on in the home screen's **Online** channel ("Online: LIGADO"). Use the game's **Xbox LIVE**
menu to play with people far away: **System Link** only finds games on your own home network.

- **Requests to the Xenia server no longer hang.** Closing each request took 55 seconds on the PS5
  (the console ignored "do not wait" on its sockets), so games gave up with "Cannot reach API
  server". It now takes under a second.
- **Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 no longer stays on a black screen** at start with online on. A
  request sent without data made the network library wait for keyboard input that never comes on
  a console. MW2 now reaches its menu and searches Xbox LIVE matches through the Xenia server.
- Requests to the server have time limits (10 s to connect, 30 s in all), so a server that does not
  answer can no longer freeze a game, and each request is written to the game's log with its
  result and time.
- Games' own non-blocking sockets now really do not wait on the PS5.
- **Router ports:** the PS5 does not let programs use ports below 1024, so a game's port 1000 is
  opened as 11000 on the console. The automatic router request (UPnP) now asks for the game's
  port towards the real one (1000 to 11000). Many routers refuse ports below 1024 that way
  (`UPnP error code 501` in the log); then add the forwarding rules by hand on the router, UDP, to
  your PS5's address: 1000 to 11000, 1001 to 11001, 1013 to 11013 (MW2's; the log's
  `XSocket::Bind` lines show each game's).

Checked on a PS5: Halo 3 online (sessions, connection checks, leaderboards) and MW2 searching
and finding other players' Xbox LIVE matches. Not confirmed yet: joining and playing a whole match
with other people. Please send the game's log from `PPSA50011/logs` with your results.

Since v0.6.0 the phone camera's certificate folder, `PPSA50011/phone-camera`, was made readable
only by the emulator, so FTP and file managers said "Permission denied" and the PPSA50011 folder
could not be deleted. Now it is made open, and starting this version once opens an existing one.

This app requires the official VitaUSBStream plugin from BMK-Studio: https://github.com/BMK-Studio/VitaUSBStream

apps.author: MisterTemaki

release.notes:
## New: GPU presentation and CRT filters

FBNeo PS5 2.4 adds Vulkan/RADV output. The CPU core generates the original game frame; the GPU handles texture scaling, CRT filtering, interface composition and final presentation.

- Eleven CRT filters now run on the GPU, including the default **CRT Easymode style**.
- Aspect ratio, smoothing, scanlines, vertical games, HUD transparency and pause-menu dimming are preserved.
- ScaleFX + rAA + AA style keeps its CPU filter with GPU presentation.
- Software output remains available: set `gpu=0` in `fbneo-ps5.ini` and restart the app. Initialization or submission failures also have software recovery paths.

Initial PS5 logs confirm **3840x2160 output at 59.940 Hz**. Sampled rates settle at **57.5 fps in Daytona USA** and **59.9 fps in Cadillacs and Dinosaurs and Contra**. Crime Fighters also starts. The observed Easymode style GPU pass takes 0.4–0.6 ms, and both logged sessions exit normally. These are initial results, not a claim of universal game/filter compatibility or native 4K game rendering.

## New: experimental two-player rollback netplay

With a compatible two-player game running, press **L3 + R3 → Netplay**. Choose **Host a game (Player 1)** on one installation, and enter its IPv4 address and matching TCP port on the other before selecting **Join a game (Player 2)**. The default port is **55435**. Both players must resume after connecting.

Use the same 2.4 build, matching ROM/BIOS content and DIP settings. This uses a direct connection between two FBNeo PS5 installations. It does not connect to Fightcade, Kaillera, RetroArch or arcade link cabinets. Games with writable hard disks are unsupported. Disconnecting restores each player's pre-session offline state; online progress is not saved.

**Netplay is experimental.** Local TCP tests and two complete Linux frontends pass real rollback/replay, pause and disconnect checks, including Vulkan output. A session between two physical PS5 consoles has not yet been validated. See the [netplay guide](https://github.com/MisterTemaki/fbneo-ps5/blob/v2.4/ps5/NETPLAY.md).

## Compatibility and stability

- Fix an audio-ring race that could read beyond the producer's input buffer.
- Handle worker-allocation failures and configuration/update I/O failures more reliably.
- Fix undefined numeric behavior in Model 2 rendering and i960 handling.
- Strengthen malformed-file, image-resize and release-update validation.
- Preserve existing saves, ROMs, settings, shader IDs and the `PPSA99924` title ID.
- Verify that the final installer contains the complete application and its dependency notices.

PC5 2.3.10 plays the films of games that use Windows Media video.

### Install

- **PC5's own updater**: **Settings › System › Update now**, or **Update now** when PC5 asks as it opens. It downloads only what changed when you have the version before, otherwise the whole app. PC5 restarts by itself when the update is installed.

### Fixed

- Games whose films are Windows Media videos (WMV) could close as the first film started; they now get the video's frame rate and play them.

### Changed

- A game's log (`about.txt`) now shows the launch options it was started with, so a report shows whether `launch.txt` was read.

### Which games run

See the [game compatibility list](https://github.com/bornaradusin/PC5/wiki/Game-compatibility), made from players' reports and issues. Got a game running? Use **Report it works** (a game's **△ › Manage**, or PC5's web page), or [add it here](https://github.com/bornaradusin/PC5/discussions/new?category=game-compatibility): the form takes a minute.

### Reporting a problem

Please report problems as an [issue on GitHub](https://github.com/bornaradusin/PC5/issues/new/choose), not in ProsperoStore's comments:
- **A game doesn't run** for a game.
- **A problem with PC5** for PC5 itself.

Attach the game's zip from `/data/prospero-win/logs/`: an `issue-…zip`, or the game's newest `log-…zip` when nothing crashed. The form asks for it, as the cause can't be found without it. **△** on PC5's crash message, or a game's **△ › Manage › Report a problem**, opens the form for you, filled in.

If an update from PC5 fails, the message says why. Turn on **Settings › System › Keep all logs**, try again and attach PC5's own log. See [Logs and debugging](https://github.com/bornaradusin/PC5/wiki/Logs-and-debugging) for what an issue may ask for.

### Not supported

- Games that need a store's launcher or client running (Steam, EA app, Ubisoft Connect, Rockstar Games Launcher).
- Anti-cheat, games that need kernel drivers, and DRM-protected games.
- .NET programs that mix .NET and C++ (C++/CLI).

## Security fixes in 01.004.001

This update fixes security holes in TokenStation5's built-in Tailscale. Update if you use Tailscale to reach your PS5 (#97).

- **Your tailnet's access rules now apply.** Before, every device on your tailnet could reach the API, whatever the rules in your Tailscale admin console said. Now only devices your rules allow can connect, and none can until the rules arrive from Tailscale.
- **A way around the API key is closed.** A device on the tailnet that opened a connection and dropped it at the right moment could be let in without a key. Over Tailscale, every request now needs a key, as intended.
- **HTTPS no longer trusts the leaked eMudhra certificates** (Tailscale's bulletin TS-2026-013), for every connection the title makes: Tailscale, downloads and search.
- **Your Tailscale sign-in key is deleted from the settings file** once the PS5 has signed in, so it can't be read later over the home network's FTP.

About "Tailworm": those flaws are in Tailscale SSH and Serve in Tailscale's own `tailscaled`. TokenStation5 runs its own small Tailscale client, without SSH or Serve, so they don't apply to it.

Tested on a PS5 over Tailscale: a valid key works for chat, and no key, a wrong key or a deleted key is refused.

- Switching models no longer fails with "out of GPU memory" after a bigger model was loaded: the model's memory is now split into smaller pieces (#94).
- A GPU check on the model you're serving no longer runs out of memory (#94).
